Scanned awesome-docker for tools matching five use cases in the Determinex
Hetzner eval pipeline. Matches recorded below; non-matches noted.

---

## Use Case 1: Container Log Aggregation / Structured Log Parsing

### Autoheal
- URL: https://github.com/willfarrell/docker-autoheal
- Use case for Determinex eval pipeline: Automatically restarts unhealthy eval
  containers that stall mid-test (OOM-killed containers leave eval jobs hanging
  indefinitely without this).
- Integration point: Deploy as a sidecar on the Hetzner node. Containers with
  `HEALTHCHECK` directives that fail get restarted automatically, preventing the
  batch script from waiting forever on a dead eval.

### dockprom
- URL: https://github.com/stefanprodan/dockprom
- Use case for Determinex eval pipeline: Prometheus + Grafana + cAdvisor stack for
  per-container CPU/memory/network metrics. Useful for diagnosing which tools are
  hitting memory limits silently (the exact problem flagged by the user).
- Integration point: Run once on Hetzner before a batch eval. Query cAdvisor
  metrics after the run to correlate tools that timed out with container memory
  usage.
- Note: Heavyweight — overkill for one-off batch runs, but ideal if Hetzner
  becomes a permanent eval node.

## Use Case 2: Parallel Container Execution / Job Queuing

No direct match found in awesome-docker for lightweight parallel job queuing
at the level Determinex needs (sequential-by-design with `PROGRAMBENCH_DOCKER_CPUS`
controlling parallelism). The existing `for tarball in submissions/*.tar.gz` loop
in `pb_hetzner_batch.py` is appropriate.

Closest match reviewed:
- **Swarm-cronjob** (https://github.com/crazy-max/swarm-cronjob): schedules Docker
  Swarm jobs on a cron schedule. Not applicable — Determinex doesn't use Swarm.
- **Mesos** (https://github.com/apache/mesos): resource/job scheduler. Overkill.

Recommendation: No external tool needed. The current sequential loop with a
600s `timeout` per tool is the right design for a shared 8-core node.

---

## Use Case 3: Container Startup Time Optimization

No direct match in awesome-docker. ProgramBench containers are pre-built by
`pb eval` during the compile phase, so startup time is dominated by Docker image
layer pulls, not runtime init.

Practical optimization (no external tool needed): pre-pull the programbench
base image on Hetzner before the batch run:
```bash
docker pull programbench/eval:latest  # or whatever base image PB uses
```
This eliminates the first-container-pull cold start (~30s per batch).

---

## Use Case 4: SCP / File Transfer Optimization for Containers

No matching tool in awesome-docker for SCP optimization. The current
`scp_to` / `scp_from` functions in `pb_hetzner_batch.py` are correct for
file sizes involved (tarballs up to ~10MB each).

Alternative not from awesome-docker: **rsync** (`rsync -avz --compress`) would
be faster than SCP for repeated uploads of similar tarballs (delta compression).
Integration point: replace `scp_to` in `pb_hetzner_batch.py` with rsync when
re-uploading modified tarballs across multiple runs.

## Use Case 5: Health Check / Monitoring for Long-Running Eval Jobs

### Autoheal (see Use Case 1)
- Also addresses this use case — HEALTHCHECK + autoheal = automatic recovery.

### DockProbe
- URL: https://github.com/deep-on/dockprobe
- Use case: Lightweight monitoring dashboard (~50MB RAM) with 6 anomaly
  detection rules and Telegram alerts. Could alert if a container's memory
  exceeds threshold (catching the silent OOM the user flagged).
- Integration point: Deploy DockProbe on Hetzner. Configure Telegram alert
  when any `programbench-*` container uses >80% of node RAM. Currently handled
  by `mem_watch.sh` watchdog, but DockProbe adds a web UI for post-run analysis.
- Note: The existing `mem_watch.sh` watchdog deployed on 2026-06-07 covers this
  use case adequately with zero overhead. DockProbe is only worth adding if
  persistent multi-run monitoring is needed.

## Summary

| Use Case | Tool Found | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Log aggregation | dockprom (Prometheus/Grafana) | Optional — add if node becomes permanent |
| Health check / restart | Autoheal | Worth deploying as sidecar |
| Parallel job queue | None | Not needed — sequential loop is correct |
| Startup optimization | None | Pre-pull base image manually |
| File transfer | None | Consider rsync for repeated runs |
| Memory alerting | DockProbe / mem_watch.sh | mem_watch.sh already deployed |
